lede: Which forecasting models work on real energy data? Load, solar, wind, power prices and fuel markets, scored with one protocol across statistical baselines, trained deep networks and zero-shot foundation models.

slices.label: Fresh track (post-2025-10 test data)
slices.note: Test data from 2025-10 onward, after the evaluated foundation models' training data was collected.

slices.label: Classic research datasets
slices.note: Several classic datasets are inside foundation-model pre-training corpora; compare with the Fresh slice.

findings: Best overall on probabilistic accuracy: toto-2.0-1b (0.584× Seasonal Naive WQL, 0.700× MASE, average rank 1.6).
Best foundation model on point accuracy: toto-2.0-1b (0.700× Seasonal Naive MASE).
Best deep model on point accuracy: DLinear (0.853× Seasonal Naive MASE).
Best statistical model on point accuracy: AutoTheta (0.927× Seasonal Naive MASE).

Median relative MASE by family, classic → fresh track: foundation 0.78→0.70, deep 1.03→0.86, statistical 1.05→1.00. A larger rise for foundation models than for trained models would point to an advantage from pre-training overlap on the classic datasets.

On eia930_load/day_ahead, the balancing authorities' own day-ahead forecasts score MASE 1.170; the best model scores 0.724 (toto-2.0-1b). Operator forecasts are excellent for most areas but some are published on a different demand basis than the actuals.
method: Fresh: live public feeds, tested on 2025-10-01 to 2026-09-30, after the training data of the evaluated foundation models was collected. Classic: widely used research datasets, last 20% of each series.
Each dataset is scored at two operational horizons, such as day-ahead and week-ahead for hourly data, or 5 and 20 trading days for daily prices.
Up to 60 non-overlapping forecast origins in the test period, shared by every model and series. Panels wider than 100 series are scored on a fixed random subset of 100 series.
Foundation models forecast zero-shot from up to 2048 past values. Deep models are trained per task on the training split and early-stopped on validation. Statistical models are refit on every window.

WQL is the weighted quantile loss over the 10-90% quantiles (a CRPS approximation). MASE scales the median forecast's error by the in-sample seasonal-naive error. Point forecasters have WQL equal to WAPE.
Per task, scores are divided by Seasonal Naive's. The table shows the geometric mean of those ratios and the average rank. Below 1.0 beats Seasonal Naive.

moirai-moe-1.0-base: too slow for the full benchmark: autoregressive decoding over patches with sample paths (~1 series/s at h=24, ~0.03 series/s at h=1008 on an L4; >40 GPU-hours); superseded by Moirai 2.0, which is evaluated. timeh2o-v1: gated weights (licence acceptance + HF token required) and non-commercial licence; needs Python >= 3.12.
attribution: Data: EIA (public domain), Energy-Charts/Fraunhofer ISE & SMARD (CC BY 4.0), AEMO, NESO, Sheffield Solar PV_Live, NYISO, ONS, ODRÉ, Energinet, NZ Electricity Authority, Elexon, World Bank, and the research datasets listed above under their own licences.
